correctness.rationale: For \(r\ge3\) and \(\lambda=r+1\), the disjoint colour sets across parts force either all monochromatic or exactly one bichromatic part. In the monochromatic type a first local force is impossible unless initial colouring is total. In the bichromatic type, no uncoloured vertex in the bichromatic part can ever see r neighbour colours, so that part must be initially fully coloured. A first force outside it is possible only when all but at most one other part is seeded; this condition is sufficient by forcing the missing part then filling remaining blanks. The resulting nonoverlapping constructions give the full count, probability formula and minimum multiplicity. The verifier independently enumerates all partial assignments for 14 profiles and matches every coefficient. Finite checking is corroboration; the unrestricted theorem rests on the argument.

originality.rationale: Compared mathematical implications rather than matching titles. The all-\(r\ge3\), palette r+1 local-forcing classification and exact polynomial are absent from the inspected initiating paper. The closest complete multipartite published theorem has palette r, and the closest surplus-palette theorem has only \(r=2\) with \(\lambda=3\). The arguments for those special settings do not imply the present first-surplus result. Historical priority is provisional because searchable literature is not complete.
residual_risks: Search incompleteness and unindexed or differently named historical prior work could contain an equivalent family formula.

value.rationale: Adding one colour to the chromatic palette creates a previously absent bicromatic-seeding obstruction in all complete multipartite graphs with three or more parts, changing minimum forcing domains and allowing an exact complete polynomial, probability function and minimizer counts for arbitrary nonuniform part sizes. This is a structural infinite-family extension of the motivating 2026 problem, not a routine transcription of the known palette-r result.
